title: M27: The Dumbell Nebula
caption: The Dumbbell Nebula (M27), imaged at the Kitt Peak Visitor Center

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: The Dumbbell Nebula, M27, is a bubble of gas thrown off by a star near the end of its life, like others of its kind. What is left of the star's core sits at the centre, visible as a slightly bluish star just above a small triangle of white stars, and it makes the bubble glow.

Surprisingly, in visible light the gas shines more brightly than the central star. The reason is that the star emits most of its light at shorter, more energetic wavelengths such as ultraviolet, which our eyes cannot see. The surrounding gas absorbs that energy and re-emits it as visible light, so we see the bubble rather than the source.

Through a small telescope or from city skies, the brighter part of the nebula looks like a half-eaten apple core, which gave it its name. From dark Kitt Peak, and in this image, the full bubble is easy to see.
scale: M27 is perhaps 1,000 light-years away, according to NOIRLab.

understand.summary: This is a visible-light image taken with a CCD camera at the Kitt Peak Visitor Center's roll-off-roof observatory, using several broadband filters. The packet does not say which colour each filter was assigned.
filters: 438 nm · Optical B (Visitor Center Roll off Roof Observatory Other CCD)
475 nm · Optical G (Visitor Center Roll off Roof Observatory Other CCD)
625 nm · Optical R (Visitor Center Roll off Roof Observatory Other CCD)
555 nm · Optical Broad Band (Visitor Center Roll off Roof Observatory Other CCD)
understand.eye: Through a small telescope the eye sees mainly the bright apple-core shape; a long camera exposure reveals the complete, fainter bubble.

explore: The nebula's age is estimated at 3,500 years. The image was made by Joe and Gail Metcalf with Adam Block through the Advanced Observing Program at the Kitt Peak Visitor Center in 2014.
alt: A glowing bubble of gas with a brighter central region, and a slightly bluish star at its centre above a small triangle of white stars.
